comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Hit again on 0.4.1, and the measurement matches this card exactly - three orphans on a devenv, 31 minutes after the ssh carrying them died, for exactly the three panes that could not re-attach:

    1708967  31:50  herdr terminal session control w4:p2 --cols 164 --rows 27
    1708971  31:50  herdr terminal session control w4:p1 --cols 164 --rows 59
    1713704  30:25  herdr terminal session control w4:p3 --cols 164 --rows 29

One correction to this card. It says "Muster's own side is fixed (kan a_2HrmSyRAQ): a replacement bridge re-attaches with --takeover." That holds only while the app that owned the dead bridges is still running. A takeover needs `bridgeRestarts > 0` for the pane, and a freshly launched app has zero for all of them, so every attach after a relaunch is a plain one and an orphan refuses all of them. Unplug and then relaunch, in that order, and Muster's side has no answer - which is the ordinary order, since a laptop that has lost its network is a laptop somebody is about to restart things on.

Filed as `a_2IQsToWVW` with the run log. It does not change what this card asks of herdr; it removes the reason to treat that ask as already worked around.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A herdr client whose stdout is a pipe to a dead sshd never notices and goes on holding the terminal it attached to. Measured on a devenv 53 minutes after the ssh carrying it had died:

    1700890  53:08  /home/.muster/bin/herdr terminal session control w1:p1 --cols 185 --rows 51
    1700895  53:08  /home/.muster/bin/herdr terminal session control w1:p2 --cols 164 --rows 43

Two orphans, for exactly the two panes that could not be re-attached afterwards. The third devenv pane in the same window had no orphan and came back normally.

Only one client may hold a terminal, so this turns one dropped connection into a pane that is permanently unusable by anything but a takeover. Muster's own side is fixed (kan a_2HrmSyRAQ): a replacement bridge re-attaches with --takeover. That works, and it is Muster papering over something the daemon could answer better - a client that finds its transport gone could exit and release the terminal, and then nobody would need the flag for this case at all.

Found while fixing a_2HrmSyRAQ during the 2026-08-31 shakedown.
title: 🔌 Upstream: a herdr client whose transport is gone holds its terminal forever
